title.rendered: Off The Beaten Path Places to Visit from Cusco

content.rendered:
Off the Beaten Path Places to Visit from Cusco

Cusco is globally renowned for its proximity to the iconic Machu Picchu, but there are numerous lesser-known gems that offer unique and enriching experiences. Beyond the well-trodden paths, you’ll find incredible destinations and organizations making a significant impact on the community. If you’re planning a trip to Cusco and want to explore beyond the usual tourist spots, here are some special places that will give you a deeper appreciation of Peru’s rich culture and breathtaking landscapes.

Sacred Valley: Dive Deeper with Llama Pack Peru

When visiting the Sacred Valley, don’t limit yourself to the well-known ruins included in the boleto turistico. To experience the area more authentically, consider taking a trip with Llama Pack Peru. This wonderful organization offers both single-day and multi-day trips that go beyond mere sightseeing.

Llama Pack Peru not only provides an immersive experience but also supports local communities in a wholesome, ethical way. You’ll trek through stunning landscapes with llamas as your companions, allowing you to connect with the environment and local culture. The organization’s commitment to sustainable tourism ensures that your visit benefits the residents and preserves the natural beauty of the Sacred Valley.

Hike Club Cusco: For the Independent Adventurer

If you’re a hiking enthusiast or someone who enjoys spontaneous adventures, joining the Hike Club Cusco community is a fantastic idea. This community offers resources for those looking to explore Cusco’s trails independently, providing maps, trail guides, and a network of fellow hikers.

Whether you’re interested in short day hikes or more challenging treks, Hike Club Cusco has something for everyone. It’s a great way to discover hidden paths, enjoy spectacular views, and experience Cusco beyond the typical tourist routes.

Manu National Park: The Hidden Jungle Gem

While Iquitos and Puerto Maldonado are more accessible via airports, Manu National Park is the true gem of the Peruvian jungle. If you seek an authentic rainforest experience, consider traveling with Hidden Jungle Cusco. This organization offers tours that provide not only a deep immersion into the jungle’s biodiversity but also contribute to protecting the founder’s family’s land.

Manu National Park spans from the High Andes down to the Reserved Zone, offering a wide range of altitudes, climates, and wildlife. It’s one of the most biodiverse places on Earth, home to giant river otters, caimans, and jaguars. Visiting this park allows you to witness wildlife in its natural habitat, learn about complex jungle ecosystems, and support conservation efforts.

The Saturday Market in Plaza Tupac Amaru: A Local Vibe

A few miles from Cusco’s Plaza de Armas, you’ll find the bustling Saturday Market in Plaza Tupac Amaru. This market offers a more local vibe compared to the central markets. On Saturdays, vendors gather to sell a variety of goods, including baked items, plants, and handcrafted products.

It’s an excellent spot to mingle with locals, purchase unique souvenirs, and enjoy a slice of Cusco’s community life. Whether you’re looking for traditional crafts or simply want to experience the local market atmosphere, Plaza Tupac Amaru is a must-visit.

Wanchaq Market: The Ultimate Caldo de Gallina

Your visit to Cusco wouldn’t be complete without trying caldo de gallina, a traditional chicken soup that’s both hearty and flavorful. Head to the Wanchaq Market to taste some of the best caldo de gallina, served with escabeche (pickled vegetables) and yucca.

On a chilly morning, this dish is a perfect way to start your day. Wanchaq Market is not just a place to eat but also a great spot to experience the local food culture and interact with the vendors.

The Positive Impact of Tourism in Cusco

Tourism in these off-the-beaten-path areas of Cusco has a generally positive impact on local communities. It creates work opportunities for locals, reducing their dependence on agriculture and encouraging the preservation of their natural environment. Supporting small, locally-owned companies ensures that your travel has a beneficial effect, helping to maintain and cherish Peru’s rich cultural and natural heritage.

Tourism reminds the locals, especially the younger generation, of the importance of their home and the surrounding nature. By choosing to travel with ethical and sustainable companies, you contribute to the conservation efforts and support the livelihoods of the communities you visit.
